atlas-sg.0001: One city, three big employers of graduates: finance, with about 200,000 jobs; tech, with more than 220,000 professionals, most of them outside tech firms; and the world’s leading container port. The work pass is the filter: the Employment Pass salary floor is above what most fresh graduates earn outside finance and tech.
atlas-sg.0004: Asia’s finance and tech headquarters city, and its busiest port
atlas-sg.0007: about 200,000 finance jobs, over 80% held by locals
atlas-sg.0008: 58.7% of tech professionals work outside tech firms
atlas-sg.0012: §4 Singapore: COMPASS arithmetic, graduate pay, tuition grants
atlas-sg.0014: §7 visas and mobility for tech graduates
atlas-sg.0015: How long the graduate Long-Term Visit Pass lasts is not stated on the ICA page read.
atlas-sg.0016: Demand in AI, data science, business and management roles is not rated: no source read measures them separately.
atlas-sg.0017: No published outcomes for coursework master’s graduates in Singapore were found; graduate surveys report bachelor’s degrees only.
atlas-sg.0018: For a European with a top-tier degree, the salary floor, not the points, is the real barrier: it sits above median bachelor’s graduate pay, so it is realistic mainly in finance, tech and consulting.
atlas-sg.0019: English is the language most often spoken at home by 48.3% of residents aged five and over (2020), up from 32.3% in 2010, and is the common language of work.
atlas-sg.0020: Resident tax rates run from 0% on the first S$20,000 to 24%; a foreigner becomes resident after 183 days, and a non-resident’s employment income is taxed at 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher.
atlas-sg.0021: Foreign employees, Employment Pass holders included, do not pay into the state pension fund (CPF); the government points them to the voluntary Supplementary Retirement Scheme instead.
atlas-sg.0022: Singapore has over 2,500 licensed financial institutions employing close to 200,000 people; over 80% of the workforce is local, and nine in ten net new jobs between 2018 and 2023 went to locals.
atlas-sg.0023: Singapore employed 222,170 tech professionals in 2025, up from 181,050 in 2020; 58.7% of tech and media staff work outside the infocomm sector.
atlas-sg.0024: The port handled a record 44.66 million TEU in 2025, up 8.6%, and was named the world’s leading container port.
atlas-sg.0026: headquartered and listed in Singapore, in 19 markets
atlas-sg.0027: owner of Garena, Shopee and Monee, founded in Singapore
atlas-sg.0030: The all-university graduate median (S$4,500 in 2025) was read only in a trade-press report of the joint survey, not on the universities’ own page; the pay claim here uses SMU’s annex.
atlas-sg.0031: Temasek, GIC, OCBC and UOB are not listed as employers because no head-office or headcount source we can cite was read.
atlas-sg.0032: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Singapore fourth in the world, one rating point behind Hong Kong in third and second in Asia/Pacific; for fintech it ranks Singapore fourth, after Hong Kong, New York and Shenzhen.
atlas-sg.0033: Startup Genome’s 2026 report ranks Singapore eighth among the world’s start-up ecosystems and second in Asia.
atlas-sg.0034: DBS says it is a leading financial services group in Asia with a presence in 19 markets, headquartered and listed in Singapore, and reports total assets of SGD 897 billion.
atlas-sg.0035: Sea Limited, founded in Singapore in 2009, runs Garena (games), Shopee (e-commerce) and Monee (digital payments and financial services); it describes Shopee as the largest pan-regional e-commerce platform in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil.
atlas-sg.0036: In 2025 another 35 maritime companies opened or expanded in Singapore, taking the total to more than 200 international shipping groups; Singapore kept its top ranking in the Xinhua-Baltic International Shipping Centre Development Index and was named the world’s leading container port by DNV-Menon.
atlas-sg.0037: In Singapore Management University’s 2025 graduate employment survey, graduates in full-time permanent jobs had a median gross monthly pay of S$4,600 in business management, S$4,500 in economics, S$4,350 in accountancy and S$5,400 in information systems, about six months after finishing.
atlas-sg.0038: Full-time employed residents with a degree had a median gross monthly income of S$9,038 in 2025, against S$5,775 for all full-time employed residents; the resident unemployment rate for professionals, managers, executives and technicians was 2.8%.
atlas-sg.0039: In the 2025 survey of the six autonomous universities, 88.9% of graduates had secured employment within six months (91.2% in 2024), 74.4% were in full-time permanent jobs and the median gross monthly salary was S$4,500; business graduates had 91.2% secured employment and a median of S$4,400.
atlas-sg.0040: Bank graduate cohorts start in July: DBS’s Management Associate Programme commences on 5 July 2027 and HSBC’s Singapore corporate and institutional banking programmes start in July 2027, with assessment centres from September to November 2026; NTU’s main career fair runs each September and February, and the Employment Pass salary floor rises on 1 January 2027.
atlas-sg.0041: Singapore’s banks, consultancies and tech firms hire graduates through internships and graduate programmes recruited mostly from NUS, NTU and SMU. For a foreigner, the gate is the work pass more than the interview: the Employment Pass needs a salary of S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance), rising to S$6,000 (S$6,600) for applications from 1 January 2027, and 40 points under COMPASS.
atlas-sg.0043: UOB’s summer internship is a full-time placement of at least 10 weeks, and strong performers may be considered for its Management Associate Programme; DBS plans to hire more than 500 young local people in 2026 across its Management Associate, internship and traineeship programmes.
atlas-sg.0044: Internships also set pay: Deloitte’s starting pay of S$4,000 to 4,500 a month varies with internship experience.
atlas-sg.0045: No conversion rate from internship to offer was found in the pages read, so this ranking rests on the employers’ own programme pages, not on a survey.
atlas-sg.0047: The local banks recruit one cohort a year: DBS’s Management Associate Programme is a 12-month permanent post that commences on 5 July 2027 with a full-day case challenge, UOB’s lasts 24 months, and HSBC’s Singapore corporate and institutional banking programmes start in July 2027 with assessment centres from September to November.
atlas-sg.0048: The Big Four take the largest classes: EY planned about 500 fresh graduates in 2025, roughly 75% from the autonomous universities, and PwC and Deloitte each hired more than 250; PwC drew more than 2,000 applications each cycle.
atlas-sg.0050: NTU’s flagship career fair is held in September for the first semester and in February for the second, and SMU’s Career Fair is held twice a year with over 100 companies in accountancy, business, economics, information systems, law and social sciences.
atlas-sg.0052: GovTech runs internships for polytechnic and university students, a Smart Nation Scholarship and a 3-year Technology Associate Programme; the Public Service Commission offers PSC Scholarships and a Master’s Scholarship that lead into the Public Service.
atlas-sg.0053: The Ministry of Education ranked second in gradsingapore’s 2026 list of leading graduate employers, behind DBS.
atlas-sg.0055: AI Singapore’s AI Apprenticeship Programme trains engineers on real projects and says over 90% of its graduates are hired, by DSTA, DBS, Grab, Capgemini and AI Singapore itself.
atlas-sg.0056: OCBC Ignite, launched in 2024, combines internships and apprenticeships leading to full-time jobs and aims to benefit 500 polytechnic students and graduates over three years.
atlas-sg.0057: Direct application on MyCareersFuture and employer sites
atlas-sg.0058: Employers must advertise on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 consecutive days, with the salary range shown, before applying for an Employment Pass for a foreign hire, so experienced hires meet a public advert and a local-first process.
atlas-sg.0059: The salary floor sits above the median pay of local bachelor’s graduates (about S$4,500 to S$4,750), so outside finance, tech and consulting few entry jobs clear it.
atlas-sg.0060: Bank cohorts start in July of the following year (DBS on 5 July 2027), so selection runs in the second half of the year before: HSBC’s July 2027 programmes hold assessment centres from September to November 2026 on a rolling basis, and applications may close early.
atlas-sg.0061: The Employment Pass salary floor rises on 1 January 2027 to S$6,000 for most sectors and S$6,600 in financial services, for new applications.
atlas-sg.0062: The local banks run one intake a year through management-associate programmes: DBS, ranked the top graduate employer in 2026, planned to hire more than 500 young locals across its programmes; UOB’s programme lasts 24 months.
atlas-sg.0063: Over 80% of the financial-sector workforce is local and more than 9 in 10 net new jobs between 2018 and 2023 went to locals; the Employment Pass salary floor for finance is S$6,200 a month today.
atlas-sg.0064: The Big Four take the largest graduate classes: EY planned about 500 fresh graduates in 2025 and now hires more computer-science and data-science graduates; PwC and Deloitte each took over 250, PwC from more than 2,000 applications a cycle, mostly from the local universities.
atlas-sg.0065: Starting pay is about S$4,300 a month at EY, from S$4,350 at PwC and S$4,000 to 4,500 at Deloitte, with about 65% of PwC’s latest cohort in audit.
